title: Velocity & Career Check — scratch prep (Ethan Lowe)
content:
Context: weekly 1:1 with my direct report (Aisha). Goal is to cover sprint velocity, unblock any infra/workflow blockers, and spend 15–20m on career coaching/check-in. This is a scratchpad; keep short prompts, decide what to follow up on after the meeting.

Meeting logistics:
- Length: 40 minutes (25m work + 15m career)
- Medium: Zoom (record for notes)
- Prep time required from them: quick status in Slack thread (1–2 bullets)

Top goals for this 1:1:
1) Get clear signal on sprint velocity drop last week. Find root cause vs surface metrics. (Is it infra? test flakiness? focus?)
2) Surface any PR/workflow friction that wastes deep work time (CI flakes, long queue times for dedicated staging).
3) Career coaching: short-term growth target + removing one organizational barrier.

Quick dashboard numbers (from sprint board / weekly report):
- Planned story points this sprint: 38
- Completed story points (so far): 19 (mid-sprint) -> projection ~36 (slip potential)
- Avg PR turnaround (review -> merge): 42h (target <=24h)
- CI flake rate (per pipeline): ~6% last week (baseline 2.2%)
- Oncall interrupts: Aisha had 3 pages (2 infra, 1 perf) last week

Hypotheses for velocity drop (talk through):
- CI flakiness causing rework and reruns (look at INF-4823 recent incidents)
- Too many simultaneous small spikes in oncall duty leading to context switching
- Blocked work waiting for infra quota from Dedicated team (INF-4901)

Agenda (40m):
1) Quick check-in (2–3m) — mood, bandwidth (ask: How's your energy? Anything urgent?)
2) Sprint health (12–15m)
   - Walk through 3 red flags: PR turnaround, CI flakes, oncall interference
   - Ask concrete: Which of these is the biggest pain on your side? Examples of wasted time this week?
   - Decide: 1 action to try this sprint to mitigate (e.g., pair on the flaky test, request temporary queue bump for dedicated staging jobs)
3) Career and growth (15m)
   - Quick signal: Are there opportunities this quarter you want more ownership over? (e.g., infra performance project, mentoring new hires)
   - Coaching prompt: "If you had one stretch project that would accelerate your next promotion, what is it and what's blocking you?"
   - Agree on 1 measurable step this quarter (deliverable + timeline)
4) Wrap & action items (3–5m)

Notes to surface during the conversation:
- PR turnaround: cite example PR (#842) where review lag added two days — ask who was the reviewer and whether reviewers are overloaded.
- CI flakes: suggest temporary tactical fix — disable flaky test in pipeline and create an Infra ticket to root cause (owner: Aisha + SRE pairing).
- Oncall: propose a short-term rotation tweak to reduce deep-work disruption (e.g., protected focus windows 10:00–13:00 for eng-platform).

Coaching script snippets (use conversational tone):
- "Tell me about a win from last sprint that you felt proud of." (starts positive)
- "If we wanted to make this work more visible for promotions, how would you frame the impact?"
- "What's one blocker that I can remove this week so you get 4 uninterrupted hours for focused work?"

Concrete action items (capture during meeting):
- Action A (owner: Ethan): Open follow-up to infra/product on quota for dedicated staging (JIRA INF-4901) and ask for an ETA. Due: 2028-03-02.
- Action B (owner: Aisha): Run binary search to reproduce CI flakes, post findings to #eng-ci and add initial note on INF-4823. Due: 2028-03-01.
- Action C (owner: Team): Experiment: one protected focus block for eng-platform team (pilot next Tues–Thu). Ethan to draft ask to SRE/People. Due: 2028-03-06.
- Action D (owner: Aisha): Draft a 2-week plan for the stretch project (owner: infra perf) to present in next 1:1. Due: 2028-03-14.

Follow-ups I should do after meeting:
- Send short summary in Slack + link to actions (within 24h).
- If CI root cause is urgent, trigger a pairing session with SRE this week and block 2 hours on both calendars.
- Re-check PR review queue metrics in 1 week; if no improvement, escalate to eng leads and propose reviewer rotation.

Open questions to ask them live (keep these handy):
- Which specific PRs caused the worst review delays? (want 1–2 examples)
- When you say "CI flake", which pipeline/step? (unit, integration, e2e)
- For the stretch project: what infrastructure access or support do you need from me and from SRE?

Quick risk/mitigation notes for me (manager):
- Risk: we try too many tactical fixes and ignore systemic reviewer overload -> Mitigate: measure reviewer load across team and propose temporary reviewer on-call rotation.
- Risk: protected focus blocks collide with team standups / customer meetings -> Mitigate: coordinate with PMs before pilot.

Post-meeting wrap template (to paste into Slack):
- TL;DR: did a quick sprint check + career discussion. Agreed actions: 1) INF-4901 follow-up (Ethan), 2) CI repro + notes (Aisha), 3) protected focus pilot (team). Will check back in next 1:1 on 2028-03-14.

Notes to self: keep the career conversation future-focused — avoid turning it into a status update. Make the ask specific: 2 deliverables, 1 mentor pairing.

End of scratchpad.
summary: Scratchpad for an engineering manager 1:1: sprint velocity troubleshooting, PR/CI friction, oncall impacts, and career coaching. Contains agenda, metrics, hypotheses, scripts, and concrete action items with owners and due dates.
